info.title: Range Monitor API
info.summary: The backend for the Range Monitor
info.description:
The backend application for Cyber Range Monitor, powered by FastAPI.

### Authentication

Authentication is done via Json Web Tokens (JWT) using the standard access and refresh
token scheme where the access token is short-lived and the refresh token is long-lived.
For every authenticated request, include the bearer access token in the `Authorization` header

```
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
```

To authenticate, create an authentication claim by sending a `POST` request to the `/auth/login`
to recieve both an access and refresh token. When the access token expires, send a `POST` request
to the `/auth/refresh` with both the expired access token and the refresh token in the request body.
Frontend clients should store the access token in memory and the refresh token in a secure, http-only cookie.

Token rotation is performed on every refresh request, meaning a new access and refresh token pair is returned
till the original refresh claim expires. Refresh claims and blacklisted tokens are stored in Redis with set
expirations to ensure they are automatically removed when expired and prevent database calls every request.
To ensure Redis remains consistent with the state of the database, a version number is stored for each user in the
database, cached in redis and embedded in the token claims. Providing an easy check constant time lookup to see if
the token is still valid.

### Roles
There are 3 roles for the Range Monitor API `admin`, `user` and `guest`.

- `guest`: The account is readonly, cannot change username or password, view other
users or change any settings.

- `user`: The account has permissions to change their username and password, view guest accounts,
create datasources and update datasources they have created. The user may not enable or disable
datasources or view other users.

- `admin`: The account has full access to the API

post.description:
Authenticates a user and issues a JWT token pair upon successful login.
The access token is to be used for authenticating API requests, while the refresh
token can be used to obtain new access tokens when the current one expires.

**protected**
Refreshes an access token using a valid refresh token
returning the rotated token claims.

get.description:
**protected**
Retrieves details about the currently authenticated access token.
The provided token must be a valid access token.

delete.description:
**protected**
Revokes the given refresh token and its associated access token.
This effectively logs the user out by invalidating their current
session tokens.
